pico: PICO: adults with type 2 diabetes; structured exercise vs usual care; outcome HbA1c; RCTs only.

title: Aerobic exercise training and glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: a randomized trial
abstract: Background: Exercise is recommended for type 2 diabetes (T2DM) management. Methods: We randomized 148 adults with T2DM (mean age 57) to a 24-week supervised aerobic exercise program (treadmill, 3 sessions/week) or usual care. The primary outcome was change in HbA1c. Results: HbA1c fell by 0.8% in the exercise group versus 0.1% with usual care (p<0.01). Conclusions: Supervised aerobic exercise improves glycemic control in adults with T2DM.

title: Resistance training versus standard care for glycemic control: a 16-week RCT
abstract: Methods: 92 adults with type 2 diabetes were randomly assigned to progressive resistance training (2x/week) or standard care for 16 weeks. HbA1c was measured at baseline and follow-up. Results: The resistance training group showed a significant HbA1c reduction (-0.6%, 95% CI -0.9 to -0.3) compared with controls. No serious adverse events occurred.

title: Combined aerobic and resistance exercise in T2DM: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: We conducted a three-arm randomized controlled trial in 210 adults with type 2 diabetes comparing combined aerobic plus resistance exercise, aerobic-only, and usual care over 26 weeks. The combined arm reduced HbA1c by 1.0% versus usual care (p<0.001); the aerobic-only arm reduced HbA1c by 0.7%.

title: High-intensity interval training improves HbA1c in type 2 diabetes: randomized trial
abstract: Sixty adults with T2DM were randomized to high-intensity interval training (HIIT, 4x4 min cycling intervals) or usual care for 12 weeks. HbA1c decreased 0.5% with HIIT versus an increase of 0.1% in controls (p=0.02). VO2peak improved 11%.

title: Tai chi for glycemic control in older adults with type 2 diabetes: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: We randomized 120 adults aged 60-75 with type 2 diabetes to tai chi classes (3x/week) or usual activity for 6 months. The tai chi group had a 0.4% greater HbA1c reduction than controls (p=0.04) and improved balance scores.

title: Home-based walking program and HbA1c in T2DM: a pragmatic randomized trial
abstract: Adults with type 2 diabetes (n=176) were randomized to a pedometer-based home walking program or usual care for 12 months. Step counts increased by 2500/day in the intervention arm; HbA1c declined 0.5% versus 0.0% in controls (p=0.008).

title: Supervised versus home-based exercise in T2DM: randomized comparison
abstract: This RCT randomized 134 adults with type 2 diabetes to supervised gym-based exercise or a home-based program, both 3x/week for 20 weeks. Supervised exercise reduced HbA1c by 0.9%, home-based by 0.4%; the between-group difference was significant (p=0.03).

title: Twelve-week circuit training in type 2 diabetes: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: We randomized 88 adults with T2DM to circuit resistance training or usual care. At 12 weeks, HbA1c was reduced by 0.7% in the training group versus 0.2% in controls (p=0.01); insulin sensitivity (M-value) improved 18%.

title: Cluster-randomized trial of community exercise referral in type 2 diabetes
abstract: Twenty-four primary care practices were cluster-randomized to an exercise referral scheme or usual care, enrolling 380 adults with type 2 diabetes. At 9 months, HbA1c was 0.3% lower in intervention practices (p=0.047).

title: Feasibility pilot RCT of aquatic exercise in obese adults with type 2 diabetes
abstract: This pilot randomized trial enrolled 36 obese adults with T2DM to aquatic exercise (2x/week, 10 weeks) or wait-list control. HbA1c fell 0.4% in the exercise arm (p=0.06). Recruitment and retention targets were met, supporting a definitive trial.

title: Post-hoc glycemic analysis of a randomized exercise trial in T2DM
abstract: We report a post-hoc analysis of a randomized controlled trial in which 150 adults with type 2 diabetes were assigned to endurance training or control for 6 months; the randomized comparison showed HbA1c reductions of 0.6% with exercise (p=0.01).

title: Dance-based exercise therapy in middle-aged adults with T2DM: an RCT
abstract: Ninety-six adults with type 2 diabetes were randomized to dance-based exercise (2x/week) or usual care for 24 weeks. HbA1c decreased by 0.6% in dancers versus 0.1% in controls (p=0.02); quality of life improved.

title: Effects of a 12-month structured exercise program on HbA1c: randomized trial
abstract: We randomly assigned 204 sedentary adults with type 2 diabetes to a structured exercise program (mixed aerobic and resistance, 150 min/week) or usual care for 12 months. HbA1c declined 0.7% with exercise versus 0.1% with usual care (p<0.001).

title: Randomized trial of morning versus evening exercise for glycemic control in T2DM
abstract: One hundred adults with type 2 diabetes were randomized to morning or evening aerobic exercise (both 5x/week, 12 weeks). Both groups improved HbA1c (morning -0.5%, evening -0.6%); no timing effect was detected (p=0.41).

title: Exercise capacity in type 1 diabetes: a randomized training study
abstract: We randomized 60 adults with type 1 diabetes to a 16-week aerobic training program or control. VO2peak improved significantly; HbA1c was unchanged. Findings apply to type 1 diabetes populations.

title: Exercise in gestational diabetes: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Pregnant women with gestational diabetes (n=120) were randomized to a supervised exercise program or standard antenatal care. Maternal fasting glucose and neonatal outcomes were assessed; HbA1c changes were modest.

title: After-school activity program for adolescents with type 2 diabetes: an RCT
abstract: We randomized 84 adolescents (aged 12-17) with type 2 diabetes to an after-school activity program or usual care for 6 months. HbA1c and BMI z-scores were measured. Adherence was the main challenge.

title: Exercise training in prediabetes: a randomized prevention trial
abstract: Adults with prediabetes (n=230) were randomized to structured exercise or control for 12 months; progression to diabetes and HbA1c were tracked. Participants with diagnosed diabetes at baseline were excluded.

title: Exercise-mimetic compounds and GLUT4 translocation in L6 myotubes
abstract: We treated L6 rat myotubes with an exercise-mimetic compound and measured GLUT4 translocation and glucose uptake in vitro. The compound increased glucose uptake 2.1-fold, suggesting therapeutic potential for type 2 diabetes.

title: Voluntary wheel running improves insulin sensitivity in diabetic mice
abstract: db/db mice were given access to running wheels for 8 weeks. Fasting glucose and insulin tolerance improved versus sedentary controls. Muscle oxidative capacity increased. Findings warrant translation to humans.

title: Physical activity and glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: a narrative review
abstract: This narrative review summarizes observational and interventional evidence linking physical activity to glycemic control in type 2 diabetes, discusses mechanisms, and offers practical recommendations for clinicians.

title: Exercise interventions for T2DM: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: We systematically reviewed randomized trials of exercise in type 2 diabetes and pooled HbA1c effects using random-effects meta-analysis (42 trials, n=3800). Pooled HbA1c reduction was -0.6% (95% CI -0.8 to -0.4).

title: Habitual physical activity and glycemic trajectories: a 10-year cohort study
abstract: In a prospective cohort of 2400 adults with type 2 diabetes, self-reported physical activity was associated with slower HbA1c rise over 10 years (adjusted beta -0.05 %/year). No intervention was delivered.

title: Gym membership and HbA1c: a cross-sectional survey
abstract: We surveyed 850 adults with type 2 diabetes about exercise habits and linked responses to most recent HbA1c values. Regular gym users had lower HbA1c (7.1% vs 7.6%, p<0.01). Causality cannot be inferred.

title: Very-low-calorie diet versus standard diet in T2DM: a randomized trial
abstract: Adults with type 2 diabetes (n=140) were randomized to a very-low-calorie diet or standard dietary advice for 20 weeks. Weight fell 11 kg versus 2 kg; HbA1c fell 1.1% versus 0.3%. No exercise intervention was studied.

title: SGLT2 inhibitor versus placebo on HbA1c in type 2 diabetes: a phase III RCT
abstract: In this double-blind trial, 700 adults with T2DM were randomized to an SGLT2 inhibitor or placebo for 26 weeks. HbA1c fell 0.9% with the drug versus 0.1% with placebo. No lifestyle intervention was included.

title: Exercise and oxidative stress in type 2 diabetes: a randomized trial
abstract: We randomized 64 adults with T2DM to aerobic exercise or control for 8 weeks. Outcomes were oxidative stress markers (8-OHdG, protein carbonyls) and VO2peak; glycated hemoglobin was not measured.

title: Protocol for a randomized trial of resistance exercise in type 2 diabetes
abstract: This protocol describes a planned two-arm randomized trial of resistance training versus usual care in 300 adults with type 2 diabetes, with HbA1c as the primary outcome. Recruitment began in 2024; results are expected in 2027.

title: Exercise training in adults with diabetes: a randomized trial
abstract: We randomized 110 adults with diabetes (62 type 2, 48 type 1) to a combined exercise program or usual care for 16 weeks. Overall HbA1c fell 0.5%; results were not reported separately by diabetes type.

note: combined lifestyle arm, exercise not separable
title: Combined diet-plus-exercise lifestyle program in T2DM: an RCT
abstract: Adults with type 2 diabetes (n=190) were randomized to a combined diet-and-exercise lifestyle program or usual care for 12 months. HbA1c fell 0.9% with the program. The relative contribution of exercise could not be isolated.

title: Alternate-week allocation study of walking in type 2 diabetes
abstract: Patients attending a diabetes clinic were allocated by alternating week of attendance to a walking program or usual care (n=150). HbA1c fell 0.4% in the walking group at 6 months (p=0.03).

title: Aqua-aerobics and glycemic control in T2DM (conference abstract)
abstract: Fifty-four adults with type 2 diabetes were randomized to aqua-aerobics or usual care for 12 weeks. HbA1c decreased 0.5% in the exercise group (p=0.04). Full text in preparation.

title: Resistance exercise and fasting glucose in T2DM: an RCT
abstract: We randomized 76 adults with type 2 diabetes to resistance training or control for 16 weeks. Fasting plasma glucose fell 1.1 mmol/L with training (p=0.01); HbA1c was not assessed in this short trial.

title: Pilot randomized trial of exergaming in adults with type 2 diabetes
abstract: This pilot RCT randomized 40 adults with T2DM to home exergaming (3x/week) or usual care for 10 weeks. HbA1c changed -0.3% versus +0.1% (p=0.09). The intervention was acceptable and safe.

note: post-hoc HbA1c subgroup of an RCT
title: Glycemic outcomes in the diabetic subgroup of a cardiac rehabilitation trial
abstract: In a post-hoc analysis of a randomized cardiac rehabilitation trial, the subgroup of 88 participants with type 2 diabetes assigned to exercise showed HbA1c reductions of 0.5% versus controls (p=0.03).

note: prospective cohort with program exposure, not randomized
title: Outcomes of a community exercise program for T2DM: prospective cohort
abstract: We followed 310 adults with type 2 diabetes who enrolled (or declined) in a community exercise program for 12 months. Enrollees showed 0.4% greater HbA1c reduction after adjustment for confounders.

title: Exercise for glycemic control across diabetes types: an umbrella review
abstract: We reviewed 15 systematic reviews of exercise interventions across type 1, type 2, and gestational diabetes. Most reported HbA1c benefits; certainty of evidence ranged from low to moderate.

title: Stepped-wedge trial of practice-nurse exercise coaching in T2DM
abstract: Using a stepped-wedge cluster randomized design, 12 clinics (n=420 adults with T2DM) crossed over to nurse-led exercise coaching. HbA1c fell 0.35% after rollout (p=0.02).

title: Acute and chronic glucose responses to exercise in T2DM: a single-arm study
abstract: Twenty adults with type 2 diabetes completed a 10-week supervised exercise program (no control group). Continuous glucose monitoring showed reduced glycemic variability; HbA1c fell 0.3% from baseline.

title: Intradialytic exercise in patients with diabetes and end-stage renal disease: an RCT
abstract: We randomized 96 adults with diabetes (84 with T2DM) receiving hemodialysis to intradialytic cycling or usual care for 6 months. Primary outcomes were physical function and dialysis adequacy; HbA1c was a tertiary outcome.
